messages:
Alex K: heads-up, after the 0.9.3 merge we're seeing a perf regression on production serving runtime. p95 downstream for chat-decode jumped ~85ms -> ~150ms and throughput dropped ~25%. noticed during canary traffic sweep. commit range: abcdef1..f7d9c3
Maria P: ugh. do we have a suspected change? any CI perf alerts? :eyes:
Alex K: CI perf did flag nightly; see ci-bot's report below. I ran a quick flamegraph on canary VMs — decode path looks thicker around attention kernel and the fused-op layer.
Tim R: can you paste the bisect result / bench script?
Alex K: ran `git bisect run ./bench/bench_decode.sh` locally. bisect pointed at f7d9c3 — "refactor attention kernels + fuse pass". local numbers: baseline (pre-merge) p95=85ms, after f7d9c3 p95=150ms, qps per-GPU down 23%.
Sam L: CI Perf bot: `https://ci.internal/reports/1750006/perf_nightly` flagged +68% p99 token latency on decode.
ci-bot: nightly perf test failed: perf_delta=+0.68, test_id=decode_path_token_latency, job=perf-nightly-1
Maria P: any idea why attention refactor would add latency? it was supposed to be faster.
Tim R: looking at the diff — they changed kernel selection heuristics to prefer the fused attention kernel even when sequence lengths are short. The fused kernel does fewer launches but does an extra memcpy to pack formats, and that memcpy shows up at runtime for short sequences as an overhead. Also the KV cache wrapper got an additional copy to align tensors.
Alex K: here's the quick flame snippet I captured (truncated):
```
flamegraph:
- decode_loop
  - attention_fused_kernel (40%)
    - memcpy (22%)
  - kv_cache_read (18%)
    - tensor_align_copy (10%)
```
Maria P: thanks. sounds like the heuristics are too eager to pick fused kernel. can we tweak the selector to check seq_len threshold? or fallback to legacy for short sequences?
Sam L: canary rollout is currently blocked by `deploy-bot`: `canary-fail: perf-regression` — product asked to hold until fixed.
deploy-bot: Canary blocked: rule perf-regression-triggered by ci-bot.
Alex K: plan: 1) revert f7d9c3 from canary to restore baseline while we iterate; 2) open a follow-up PR that adjusts kernel selection: require seq_len >= 128 for fused kernel or measure estimated memcpy cost vs launch cost; 3) add unit perf tests to CI to catch this.
Tim R: +1 for revert. quick revert PR: `git revert --no-commit f7d9c3 && ./scripts/bench_ci.sh`
Maria P: I can cut the revert PR and land it to canary-only branch. I will include perf numbers in the PR description.
Alex K: I opened rollback PR #4021 (revert f7d9c3). pasted benches: pre-merge p95=86ms, post-merge p95=149ms, post-revert p95=88ms.
Sam L: CI updated: perf-nightly now green after rollback on canary branch.
ci-bot: perf-nightly job success: perf_delta=-0.02, job=perf-nightly-1
Maria P: great — can we also add a microbenchmark that runs short-seq workloads to prevent future regressions? put it in perf/unit/short_seq.yml.
Tim R: I'll own the kernel selector patch. initial idea: cost_model(seq_len, batch) -> choose fused if saving > memcpy_cost + launch_overhead. add a cached threshold table tuned from offline runs.
Alex K: filing follow-up ticket: RN-1257 "attention fused kernel mis-selection for short sequences" assigning Tim. link: https://redwood.internal/issue/RN-1257
Sam L: note for postmortem: include bisect commands and CI test diff.
Maria P: thanks everyone. keeping this thread for audit — I'll update when rollback is fully propagated to host fleets. :thumbsup:
Alex K: rollback finished on canary, scheduling gradual rollback to prod after quick smoke tomorrow.
Sam L: marking incident as resolved-for-now, will reopen if perf reappears.
